title: A proof of the Berkovich-Dhar conjecture modulo three
summary: Let $P_n(q)=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-q^{3j-2})(1-q^{3j-1})$. For each $p\in\{4,5,6,7,8\}$, we prove that the coefficients of $P_n(q)^p$ in residue class $0$ modulo $3$ are nonnegative, and that those in residue class $2$, after zero terms are omitted, change sign exactly once, from positive to negative. The residue-$0$ coefficients are in fact strictly positive for $5\le p\le8$. This proves Conjecture 2.1 of Berkovich and Dhar in full.
